data.narrative:
Mesh Optical Technologies is a Series A semiconductor company founded by Travis Brashears, Cameron Ramos, and Serena Grown-Haeberli. The company has raised $50M to date. The valuation universe includes 3 public semiconductor peers (ALAB, NVDA, AMD) and 8 private peers in the Chips & Semiconductors sector, including SambaNova Systems, Cerebras, and Credo Semiconductor.

Stage-progression analysis was the sole applicable triangulation method. Using total capital raised of $50M as a proxy for post-money valuation and applying a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical of Series A to subsequent stage transitions yields an implied valuation of $100M. Peer-median comparison was not viable; while 12 same-sector private peers exist, filtering for same-stage, adjacent-stage, or similar-tier companies yielded fewer than three comparable datapoints. Public-comp anchoring could not be applied due to absence of revenue data for the private target, despite a median 21.5x price-to-sales multiple across the three public semiconductor comps.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $85M to $115M, with a median point estimate of $100M. This range reflects reliance on a single method and carries material uncertainty. Key risks include the limited comparability of the peer set and dependence on stage-typical multiples rather than target-specific fundamentals. Revenue disclosure or identification of tighter private peer comparables would strengthen confidence in this range.
